parsed.explanation: The combined regime imposes traveller-facing exposures at several stages. Entry screening flags document/sex discrepancies, and the national cable directs refusal and possible lifetime ineligibility for material misrepresentation; neighbouring citizens have been detained over visa issues and multiple governments issued advisories. The division's March 2025 statute bars trans people from bathrooms, locker rooms, dormitories, shelters and prisons — a universal-exposure facility exclusion with no documented remedy and a religious-refusal law permitting service denial. Detention carries documented severe harm (conversion-style practices, forced labour, sexual abuse). Offsetting factors exist but are resident-facing or climate signals: national hate-crime coverage, national employment protection, no criminalisation of trans identity. No documented arrest under this state's facility statute, and enforcement patterns are unsourced, so severity is rated on the possibility every outed traveller carries.

entry_documents.exposure: National policy refuses cases with sex discrepancies, may find material misrepresentation supporting permanent lifetime ineligibility; trans travellers report passports blocked/confiscated and stranding; detentions of neighbouring citizens reported.
entry_documents.protection: Fraud finding is never automatic, requires four elements, and waiver possibilities exist; policy is under litigation.
entry_documents.interaction: Screening touches every visitor's documents and feeds directly into detention/removal decisions at the border.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody: trans men report forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse; national corrections adopt conversion-style policies (hair cutting, hormone removal, psychiatric substitution).
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Consular access; national hate-crime statute covering gender identity; litigation ongoing.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A document-discrepancy or visa inquiry can escalate into immigration detention, where placement and treatment are documented as harmful.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Division statute defines only male/female and bars trans people from bathrooms, locker rooms, dormitories, rape crisis centres, shelters and prisons in government-owned settings; national map shows facility bans across many states, four criminalising in circumstances.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Some states have no ban; this statute carries no sourced penalty or documented enforcement.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Universal at the state level: any visit to a government building or shelter puts an outed traveller at risk of ejection or trespass process.

care_services.exposure: Division bans gender-affirming care for minors; adult insurance exclusion upheld on appeal and under challenge; religious-refusal statute permits denial of service, housing and government services.
care_services.protection: Emergency care not documented as denied; 15 cities bar gender-identity discrimination in public accommodations.
care_services.interaction: A visitor needing a routine refill or emergency ward placement faces discretionary refusal and possible ward misplacement.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups for rapid neutralisation; justice department reward guidance invokes 'radical gender ideology'; executive orders target teachers and care providers.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The same strategy disclaims targeting mere disagreement; several orders enjoined in court.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Rhetoric raises the probability that police contact treats trans presence as suspicious rather than protected.

minors_guardians.exposure: Division bans puberty blockers, hormones and surgery for minors; a bill passed both chambers to require immediate outing of trans students to parents; national order directs prosecution of teachers using preferred names.
minors_guardians.protection: Final status of the outing bill unresolved; court injunctions on several national orders.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling family with a trans minor faces outing to guardians and foreclosed care access; the parent becomes the investigated facilitator.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No statewide non-discrimination protection; service refusal permitted on religious grounds with qualified immunity; local ordinances targeted for nullification.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National gender-identity hate-crime statute; 15 municipal ordinances; marriage recognition unaffected.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police called to a facility or service dispute would have no state-level discrimination ground to act on.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Only municipal protections and a national hate-crime statute; nullification bill and outing bill pending; enforcement of facilities statute unsourced.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Litigation active on passport markers, athletics, adult insurance exclusion; legal-aid FAQ maintained.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse depends on municipality and on unsettled litigation, so a traveller cannot rely on any single protection.

anchor_checks.comparison: In 0.35-C border agents expose and deny entry but are barred from detention. Here denial and stranding are documented, plus lifetime-ineligibility findings and documented immigration-custody abuse, plus a universal facilities ban — materially worse.

In 0.45-B a clinic refuses service with only a slow appeal. Here refusal is broader (shelters, accommodations, services under the religious-refusal law) and backed by a state statute excluding trans people from facilities, with custody harm behind it — clearly lower.

In 0.25-B coerced custody and threats of imprisonment occur without legal footing. Here the coercion is codified: statutory facility exclusion, screening rules carrying lifetime ineligibility, and documented abusive detention, though no trans identity crime — comparable severity, more state-imposed and systemic.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime combines a national entry-screening posture that can refuse or permanently bar a traveller whose documents mismatch, with a state statute removing trans people from bathrooms, dormitories, shelters and prisons. Enforcement of the state statute is undocumented in practice, but detention — where the record shows conversion-style treatment and abuse — is the tail risk that document friction feeds into. Protection is thin: municipal ordinances, a national hate-crime statute, and litigation that has not yet settled the document rules. Nothing in the dossier records a working remedy for a trans visitor excluded from a facility or refused service.
